caption:
Ugh. Ending my senior season early from an ACL tear was never how I envisioned my last year of soccer. I’ve always dreamed of being in the position and role that I had this year, and it breaks my heart knowing it was cut short—but I’m trying to remember that everything happens for a reason.

Regardless, I can’t explain how thankful I am for the past four years, and if I could do it all over again, I wouldn’t change a thing. They don’t lie when they say the people make the place, and I’ve never felt so grateful than to walk away from this experience with the friendships I’ll have for the rest of my life.

Most importantly, thank you to my parents. In the 18 years I’ve been playing soccer, there are very few games I can remember them missing. Whether it was at home, in a different state, or a different country, they did everything to be at every single game and have always been my biggest support system and fans since the first day I stepped on a soccer field.

To my team, I LOVE YOU. There isn’t another team I could imagine spending my last year with, and I can’t wait to root you guys on for the rest of the season and the rest of your collegiate careers.

September is suicide awareness month. I hold this month close to my heart because of how suicide has affected me and my family. I often hold guilt for the loved ones I’ve lost, replaying countless “what if” and “if only” scenarios; often making me question my own life and worth. Last summer I struggled heavily with suicide ideations, and I fought with myself for a long time over that. I battled self harm, self confidence, and my purpose here. Usually finding myself spiraling about how I’d rather give everything up than push through. However, I won’t allow it to define who I am or take away my freedom and love. Life is full of beautiful things and people, and I have yet to find my potential.

Being open about my struggles with mental health is something I make sure to share. Everyday I make strides to improve myself and share uncomfortable truths I hold. It’s not easy but I hope it helps one less person feel alone, or one more person gain the confidence to reach out. 

I love y’all.

my goodbye to wsu💌

caption:
Thirteen years of running in red ❤️🖤🩶🤍

Finishing dead last at the first round of nationals was not what I had envisioned for the end of this chapter. It stings (bad), but I know it does not define these 13 years of running in schools from 6th grade to 6th year super-super senior.

I walk away from this ending with incredible pride and gratitude. This sport has given me everything: life long friends, an education, travels to 9 states, mentors & teachers, countless lessons, and more memories than I know what to do with.

I went from a small town girl running 2:13 and 57 to a power 5 athlete running 2:06 and 55. I ran every running event from 100m-6k. I worked through mental battles and physical injuries, and I grew in confidence, faith, discipline, and self love. 

But more than anything, I hold dear the people I’ve met on this journey and the endless ways they have impacted me. My track journey would have been nothing without the teammates, coaches, and support staff who I shared it with. Thank you SLV, thank you Seattle U, and thank you WSU for a combined 13 blessed years.

My college running days may be over, but my journey with track is not done yet; the question is only what colors I’ll be wearing next… 🌈✨✌🏼

“Not only that, but we rejoice in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces endurance, and endurance produces character, and character produces hope, and hope does not put us to shame, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us.”
‭‭Romans‬ ‭5‬:‭3‬-‭5‬

This past season was full of highs and lows, moments of success, moments of failure, moments of triumph and moments of adversity. But one thing that remained true through the midst of all of it was the commitment of these players, coaches and families to this program. There were few things this fall that brought me as much joy as showing up every day and going to work with the teammates and coaches that I love. I thank God for this season and everything that came with it. The Lord has taught me so much in this football season. He reminded me that wins and losses come and go and stats are eventually forgotten, but Jesus is the only thing that truly lasts in this world. He is the only thing in which we can find true fulfillment. In John 10:10 Jesus says, “I have come that you may have life, and have it abundantly”. This season reminded me that only in Christ can we find abudant life. Football is a gift that He has given us to glorify Him, but one day it will end. God never will.

I am so thankful for everything God has done for this football program. But even more than that, I am so incredibly grateful for His gift of salvation. How He came down as a servant, lived a perfect life, and died a death we could never imagine just so that every single one of us could find new life in Him. Though we did nothing to deserve it, He humbled Himself so that we could spend eternity with Him. My biggest hope is that my time in the Norman North football program honored the Lord in every way.

I cannot express how grateful I am for the last 4 years. I will forever be a Norman North Timberwolf🐺🐺

Threaten our Existence, Expect our Resistance - MMIWUSA

Indigenous women are ten times more likely to be killed than the average national murder rate. There are more than 5,700 cases of missing or murdered Native women documented with murder being the 3rd leading cause of death for Native American women. 

All I ask is, why?

Why do some feel the need to hunt indigenous women who are proud to represent their heritage?Why do some strip them of their freedom and innocence? I do not know them, but they are my sisters. Moreover, my sisters do not deserve this. We do not deserve to be hunted for our history and our cultural values. 

We will never be silent again. 

No more stolen sisters.
